question: A tall pea plant of unknown genotype is crossed with a pure homozygous dwarf pea plant (tt). Exactly 50% of the progeny are tall and 50% are dwarf. What was the genotype of the parent tall plant?
explanation: This is a classical test cross: Tt × tt. The gametes from Tt are T and t (50% each), and from tt are only t. The resulting offspring are 50% Tt (Tall) and 50% tt (Dwarf). If the parent were pure TT, 100% of offspring would have been tall.

question: A pea plant has the heterozygous dihybrid genotype RrYy (Round Yellow). How many genetically distinct types of gametes will it produce, and in what percentage?
options: 2 types of gametes (RY and ry) at 50% each
4 types of gametes (RY, Ry, rY, ry) in equal 25% proportions each
8 types of gametes in variable percentages
explanation: Because alleles R/r and Y/y assort independently during meiosis, the possible allele combinations in gametes are RY, Ry, rY, and ry, each produced with an equal probability of 1/4 (25%).

question: In Mendel's dihybrid cross between Round Yellow (RRYY) and Wrinkled Green (rryy) seeds, what fraction of the total 16 F2 progeny exhibit new recombinant phenotypes (phenotypes different from both original parents)?
explanation: Total F2 ratio is 9 Round Yellow (parental) : 3 Round Green (recombinant) : 3 Wrinkled Yellow (recombinant) : 1 Wrinkled Green (parental). The new recombinant phenotypes are 3 + 3 = 6 out of 16 (or 3/8).

question: In pea plants, tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t). Phenotypically, how does a homozygous tall plant (TT) compare visually to a heterozygous tall plant (Tt)?
options: TT is twice as tall as Tt
Tt has short leaves while TT has long leaves
They look identical in height because a single dominant 'T' allele is sufficient to express full tallness
explanation: In complete dominance, the presence of one dominant allele (T) produces the identical outward phenotype as two dominant alleles (TT). Thus, TT and Tt plants are indistinguishable in physical height.

question: In garden peas, violet flower color (V) is dominant over white flower color (v). If a homozygous violet-flowered plant (VV) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (vv), what will be the flower color in the F1 generation?
explanation: All F1 offspring inherit genotype Vv. Because violet (V) is completely dominant over white (v), 100% of the F1 generation will bear violet flowers.

question: A dwarf pea plant (tt) is short in stature because a mutation in the height gene causes:
options: Cell walls to become completely impervious to sunlight
An enzyme involved in plant growth hormone synthesis to be less efficient or non-functional, resulting in insufficient hormone production
The plant to lose all its root hairs
explanation: Genes synthesize enzymes that catalyze biochemical pathways. If the gene has an alteration (mutation), the enzyme synthesized is less efficient, producing less growth hormone (gibberellin), so the plant remains short (dwarf).

question: In a normal human skin epithelial cell, how many total autosomes are present?
explanation: Human diploid somatic cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs): 22 pairs (44 chromosomes) are autosomes that control general body characteristics, and 1 pair (2 chromosomes) are sex chromosomes.

question: In birds, the mechanism of sex determination is ZZ-ZW. Male birds have two identical sex chromosomes (ZZ) and females have two different sex chromosomes (ZW). In birds, which parent determines the sex of the chick?
options: The mother (female bird), because female ova carry either a Z or a W chromosome
The first hatched egg in the nest
explanation: In birds, the female is heterogametic (ZW) producing two types of eggs (50% Z and 50% W), while the male is homogametic (ZZ) producing only Z sperms. Thus, in birds, the female parent determines the sex of the offspring.

question: A father has blood group A (genotype Iᴬi) and a mother has blood group B (genotype Iᴮi). What are the possible blood groups of their biological children?
options: Only blood group A and B
All four blood groups are possible: A, B, AB, or O (25% chance each)
explanation: The father produces gametes with Iᴬ and i; the mother produces gametes with Iᴮ and i. The four possible zygotic genotypes are IᴬIᴮ (group AB), Iᴬi (group A), Iᴮi (group B), and ii (group O), each with a 25% statistical probability.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 8, Section 8.2 (In-text questions)

question: What is the chromosomal constitution of a normal, viable human sperm cell that will result in the conception of a male child?
explanation: Sperms are haploid gametes containing 23 single chromosomes. A sperm carrying 22 autosomes + Y fuses with an ovum (22 + X) to produce a male zygote with 44 + XY (46 chromosomes).

question: In Figure 8.1 of NCERT showing asexual reproduction over three successive generations, how do variations accumulate over time?
options: All variations revert back to the original ancestor DNA
Each daughter generation inherits all the ancestral variations from previous generations plus new unique mutations created during its own DNA replication
explanation: Diversity arises during asexual reproduction due to minor errors in DNA copying. In the next generation, daughter cells inherit these established differences and accumulate additional new variations, resulting in increasing diversity over generations.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 8, Section 8.1 (Figure 8.1: Creation of diversity over succeeding generations)

question: Unlike male sperms which are of two chromosomal types (X or Y), all normal human ova (eggs) produced by a woman are chromosomally:
options: Identical: 22 autosomes + one X chromosome (22 + X)
explanation: Human females have two X chromosomes (XX). During oogenesis meiosis, every ovum receives 22 autosomes and one X chromosome. Females are therefore homogametic.

question: How did Mendel establish 'pure-breeding' (true-breeding) lines of pea plants before starting his hybridization crosses?
options: By self-pollinating pea plants over several successive generations until offspring showed constant, unvarying trait expression
By growing plants in nutrient-free sand
explanation: A true-breeding line is one that, having undergone continuous self-pollination, shows stable trait inheritance and expression through several generations. This ensured homozygous parental genotypes (TT or tt).

question: What is the specific genetic function of the Y chromosome in determining male development in human embryos?
options: It manufactures testosterone inside maternal blood
It dissolves the mother's X chromosome
It prevents the embryo from implanting in the uterus
It carries the SRY gene which triggers the indifferent embryonic gonads to develop into testes instead of ovaries
explanation: The human Y chromosome carries the SRY (Sex-determining Region Y) gene. In early embryonic development, the SRY protein acts as a master switch that directs the bipotential gonads to differentiate into testes.

question: What does Mendel's First Law (Law of Segregation) state regarding the distribution of alleles into gametes?
options: All alleles blend together like mixed paint
Dominant alleles destroy recessive alleles inside gametes
The two alleles of a gene pair separate during gamete formation so that each gamete carries only one allele for that trait
Alleles cannot separate once brought together
explanation: The Law of Segregation states that during meiosis, the two alleles of each gene locus segregate from each other so that each gamete receives only one allele with equal probability.

question: A child has blood group O. If the mother has blood group A and the father has blood group B, what must be the exact genotypes of both parents?
explanation: A child with blood group O has the homozygous recessive genotype 'ii'. To produce an 'ii' child, each parent must contribute one recessive 'i' allele. Therefore, the mother must be heterozygous A (Iᴬi) and the father heterozygous B (Iᴮi).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 8, Section 8.2 (In-text questions)

question: In the F2 generation of a dihybrid cross involving two independently assorting heterozygous parents (RrYy × RrYy), how many total squares (zygotic combinations) are represented in the Punnett checkerboard?
explanation: Because each dihybrid parent produces 4 types of gametes (RY, Ry, rY, ry), the resulting Punnett square cross contains 4 × 4 = 16 zygotic boxes.

question: Which seed color in pea plants is dominant, and which is recessive according to Mendel's experiments?
options: Green seed color is dominant; Yellow seed color is recessive
Yellow seed color is dominant; Green seed color is recessive
Both are codominant yielding striped seeds
Seed color in peas is completely random
explanation: In garden peas, Yellow seed color (Y) is dominant over Green seed color (y).

question: Which seed shape in pea plants is dominant, and which is recessive according to Mendel's experiments?
options: Wrinkled seed shape is dominant; Round seed shape is recessive
Oval seed shape is dominant over square seeds
Both round and wrinkled are dominant
Round seed shape is dominant; Wrinkled seed shape is recessive
explanation: Round seed shape (R) is dominant over Wrinkled seed shape (r).

subtopic: Independent Inheritance of Blood Group and Height
question: A man with blood group A and tall stature marries a woman with blood group O and short stature. The inheritance of blood group and height in their children will be:
options: Strictly linked so that tall children must always have blood group O
Blended into a single intermediate trait
Completely independent of each other because the gene for blood group and the gene for height are located on different chromosomes
explanation: Traits governed by genes situated on different chromosomes assort independently during meiosis (Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment). Thus, height and blood group are inherited without influencing each other.
